source_text:
Χῆραι μὴ ἀμελείσθωσαν: μετὰ τὸν κύριον σὺ αὐτῶν φροντιστὴς ἔσο. μηδὲν ἄνευ γνώμης σου γινέσθω μηδὲ σὺ ἄνευ θεοῦ τι πρᾶσσε, ὅπερ οὐδὲ πράσσεις: εὐστάθει.
πυκνότερον συναγωγαὶ γινέσθωσαν: ἐξ ὀνόματος πάντας ζήτει.
δούλους καὶ δούλας μὴ ὑπερηφάνει: ἀλλὰ μηδὲ αὐτοὶ φυσιούσθωσαν, ἀλλ’ εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ πλέον δουλευέτωσαν, ἵνα κρείττονος ἐλευθερίας ἀπὸ θεοῦ τύχωσιν. μὴ ἐράτωσαν ἀπὸ τοῦ κοινοῦ ἐλευθεροῦσθαι, ἵνα μὴ δοῦλοι εὑρεθῶσιν ἐπιθυμίας.
thought_title: Care for widows, slaves, and the church's gatherings
orientation: Ignatius is giving direct instructions to Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, about how to order the church's life.
pass_a_gloss: Widows must not be neglected: after the Lord, you yourself must be their caretaker. Nothing must happen without your judgment, and you yourself must do nothing without God, which indeed you do not do: be steadfast. Gatherings must happen more frequently: seek everyone by name. Do not despise male slaves and female slaves: but neither must they themselves become conceited, but let them serve more for the glory of God, so that they may obtain a better freedom from God. They must not desire to be freed from the common fund, so that they may not be found slaves of desire.

choices.why: The noun denotes one who takes thought for or looks after others; 'caretaker' keeps the personal responsibility on Polycarp without importing a formal office.
In Ignatius, γνώμη is the bishop's considered decision or approval; 'judgment' preserves the deliberative sense rather than a mere opinion.
The word here means the church's assemblies for worship; 'gatherings' avoids the Jewish institutional sense of 'synagogue' while keeping the collective meeting idea.
The verb means to look down on or treat with contempt; 'despise' captures the attitude of superiority toward slaves that Ignatius forbids.
The verb literally means 'be puffed up'; 'become conceited' renders the moral sense of pride or self-importance in plain English.
The phrase refers to the church's shared resources used to purchase freedom for slaves; 'common fund' makes the economic sense explicit.

pass_b_english: Do not neglect the widows. After the Lord, you yourself must be their caretaker. Let nothing happen without your judgment, and do nothing yourself without God. Indeed, you do not do so. Be steadfast.
Let the church meetings take place more frequently. Seek out everyone by name.

Do not despise slaves, whether men or women. But they too must not become conceited. Instead, let them serve all the more for the glory of God, so that they may obtain a better freedom from God. They must not long to be freed at the church's expense, lest they be found slaves of desire.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'common fund' but 'common' alone is ambiguous; however brief has no fixed term for κοινόν. Re-check: no glossary entry. But 'common fund' is standard for τοῦ κοινοῦ in Ignatius. 'Common' alone loses the financial sense.
last_rejected.fix: They must not long to be freed from the common fund
last_rejected.ruling: τοῦ κοινοῦ = 'the common (fund)'; 'common fund' captures financial sense. No glossary entry broken.

last_rejected.why: 'Desire' is too neutral; ἐπιθυμίας here means sinful lust/craving, not neutral desire.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπιθυμίας includes desire/craving/lust; 'desire' is within normal range. Not a meaning change.

problems.quote: They must not long to be freed from the common fund
problems.why: 'Common fund' for slavery manumission is confusing; the Greek likely refers to church community.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'freed at the church's expense' or 'from the common fund of the church.'

edits.old: They must not long to be freed from the common fund
edits.new: They must not long to be freed at the church's expense

problems.quote: Let nothing happen without your judgment, and do nothing yourself without God—which indeed you do not do.
problems.why: Final clause 'which indeed you do not do' is awkwardly placed; seems to negate the command.
problems.fix: 'Which indeed you already do' or note that Greek may affirm Polycarp's practice.

problems.quote: Let the gatherings take place more frequently
problems.why: 'Gatherings' (synaxeis) refers to Eucharistic assemblies, not casual meetings.
problems.fix: 'Let the Eucharistic assemblies be held more frequently.'

edits.old: Let the gatherings take place more frequently.
edits.new: Let the Eucharistic assemblies take place more frequently.

fixed: The final clause 'which indeed you do not do' is not a mistranslation; the Greek 'ὅπερ οὐδὲ πράσσεις' means 'which indeed you do not do,' and the English renders it accurately. The awkwardness is stylistic, not a meaning error, so no edit is made.
The Greek 'συναγωγαί' here refers to the church's liturgical assemblies, specifically the Eucharistic gathering, so 'Eucharistic assemblies' is the correct rendering.

polish.changed: Clarified the awkward final clause about acting without God, made the Eucharistic assemblies explicit, and smoothed sentence flow for reading aloud.

notes.quote: Let nothing happen without your judgment, and do nothing yourself without God—which indeed you do not do.
notes.why: Final clause 'which indeed you do not do' is awkwardly placed; seems to negate the command.
notes.fix: 'Which indeed you already do' or note that Greek may affirm Polycarp's practice.

notes.quote: Let the gatherings take place more frequently
notes.why: 'Gatherings' (synaxeis) refers to Eucharistic assemblies, not casual meetings.
notes.fix: 'Let the Eucharistic assemblies be held more frequently.'

polish.changed: Clarified that the assemblies are the gathered church meetings, kept the direct address to the bishop consistent, and preserved every command and qualification while smoothing the English for reading aloud.

notes.quote: the virgins who are called widows
notes.why: 'Virgins who are called widows' is paradoxical; may mean 'widows who live as virgins' or an order of widows.
notes.fix: Add note: '[an order of dedicated widows who remained unmarried]'.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'assemblies' refers to church meetings, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving every instruction and qualification.

notes.quote: Let the assemblies take place more frequently
notes.why: 'Assemblies' translates Greek 'synaxis' but may seem to mean political gatherings; in context means Eucharistic meetings.
notes.fix: Change to 'Let the Eucharistic assemblies' or add note.
